correctness.rationale: Block calculation gives unique B, exact equations P squared zero and PY=YP; rank AB = rank P; rank B=2 rank P + rank induced Y on kerP/imP by image-projection exact sequence. Gaussian image/kernel-flag count enumerates square-zero P; its linear centralizer dimension is the sum of the squares of the two Jordan column lengths, and surjection onto End(kerP/imP) has constant fiber the fixed homology-fiber cardinality. Multiplication by the exact rank-u endomorphism count proves formula and support, independently of prime characteristic. Algebraic geometry follows from vector bundles over the smooth nilpotent orbit and determinantal rank strata. Direct enumeration for r=1,2,3 and q=2,3,5, plus all 65536 binary 4x4 matrices, matches predictions. Computational tests are finite corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Direct inspection of Levy 2006 identifies known characteristic-two component geometry, expressly credited; Chen–Wang 2018 contributes anticommutation block structure; Basili–Iarrobino 2007 addresses different nilpotent geometry. Their stated results do not entail the new formula counting every rank(B),rank(AB) fiber over every finite field; the centralizer-to-homology surjection and Gaussian-rank refinement add information. Actual mathematical-record searches found no equivalently quantitative claim, while the inaccessible Ngai thesis and uninspected full-text papers remain explicitly unresolved priority risks, not falsely certified negatives.

value.rationale: The fixed maximal-square-zero first action defines a canonical natural fiber in the representation variety of the two-generator exterior-type algebra. Both ranks are intrinsic module statistics, and their complete joint enumerative law is stronger than a dimension/component classification; the induced arbitrary homology matrix explains the whole distribution. Every natively feasible rank pair is covered with an exact formula for all finite fields and smoothness/dimension of its geometric stratum. The exact counts plausibly assist point-counting, representation distributions and further component studies; no unsupported downstream theorem is claimed.
